check_registry_exists() {
  log "Check 1: Registry exists and is valid JSON"

  if [[ ! -f "$REGISTRY" ]]; then

  if ! jq empty "$REGISTRY" 2>/dev/null; then

  local count
  count=$(jq '.constraints | length' "$REGISTRY")
  pass "Registry is valid JSON with $count constraints"

}

# ============================================================================

  log "Check 2: Schema compliance"

  if [[ ! -f "$SCHEMA" ]]; then

    return 1
  fi

  if command -v ajv &>/dev/null; then

      pass "Schema validation passed (ajv)"
      return 0

  local errors=0

  # Check top-level required fields
  if ! jq -e '.version and .constraints' "$REGISTRY" >/dev/null 2>&1; then

  # Check version pattern
  local version

  if ! [[ "$version" =~ ^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$ ]]; then
    fail "Invalid version format: $version"
    errors=$((errors + 1))

  # Check each constraint has required fields

  missing=$(jq -r '

      (.id | not) or (.name | not) or (.category | not) or

      (.layers | not) or (.severity | not)
    ) | .id // "UNKNOWN"] | join(", ")
  ' "$REGISTRY")

  if [[ -n "$missing" ]]; then
    fail "Constraints missing required fields: $missing"
    errors=$((errors + 1))
  fi

  # Check ID pattern
  local bad_ids
  bad_ids=$(jq -r '[.constraints[] | select(.id | test("^C-[A-Z]+-[0-9]{3}$") | not) | .id] | join(", ")' "$REGISTRY")

     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/check-knob-readers.sh — no direct read of a profile key outside
     4	# profile-lib.sh (cycle-129 SDD D-9.1, sprint-256 Task 2.7).
     5	#
     6	# Every key under any profile in .claude/data/profiles.yaml must be read
     7	# through `loa_knob` (.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh), never by a reader's
     8	# own `yq '.<key> // <default>'`: a direct read skips the profile, and yq's
     9	# `//` reads an explicit `false` as absent. The check flags a line that names a
    10	# profile key in yq-path form (a leading dot: `.guardrails.input.enabled`)
    11	# under .claude/ (scripts, hooks, skills, data) and tools/, except
    12	# profile-lib.sh itself. Prose that names a key without the dot
    13	# (`guardrails.input.enabled: false`) is not a read and is not flagged.
    14	#
    15	# Misses: a key assembled at runtime (".guardrails.input.${x}.enabled") and a
    16	# reader in a language that indexes the config as nested keys.
    17	#
    18	# Usage: tools/check-knob-readers.sh [--root DIR]
    19	# Exit:  0 clean · 1 direct read found (each printed as path:line) · 2 usage
    20	# =============================================================================
    21	set -euo pipefail
    22	export LC_ALL=C
    23	
    24	ROOT="."
    25	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    26	  case "$1" in
    27	    --root) [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: --root needs a directory" >&2; exit 2; }; ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    28	    -h|--help) sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit:/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0 ;;
    29	    *) echo "check-knob-readers.sh: unknown arg $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    30	  esac
    31	done
    32	PROFILES="$ROOT/.claude/data/profiles.yaml"
    33	[[ -f "$PROFILES" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: $PROFILES not found" >&2; exit 2; }
    34	command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: yq v4 required" >&2; exit 2; }
    35	
    36	keys=$(yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' "$PROFILES" | sort -u)
    37	[[ -n "$keys" ]] || { echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no profile keys in $PROFILES" >&2; exit 2; }
    38	# Alternation of the dot-escaped keys; each must be preceded by a dot that is
    39	# not itself part of an identifier (start of line, quote, space, paren, ...).
    40	alt=$(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | sed 's/\./\\./g' | paste -sd'|' -)
    41	pattern="(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])\\.(${alt})([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)"
    42	
    43	hits=$(cd "$ROOT" && grep -rnE "$pattern" .claude tools 2>/dev/null \
    44	  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?\.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib\.sh:' \
    45	  | grep -v -E '^(\./)?tools/check-knob-readers\.sh:' || true)
    46	if [[ -n "$hits" ]]; then
    47	  echo "check-knob-readers.sh: direct read(s) of a profile key; use loa_knob from .claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:" >&2
    48	  printf '%s\n' "$hits" | cut -c1-240 >&2
    49	  exit 1
    50	fi
    51	echo "check-knob-readers.sh: no direct profile-key reads ($(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | wc -l | tr -d ' ') keys checked)"

input.command: cd /workspace/pr; keys=$(yq -r '.profiles[] | keys | .[]' head/.claude/data/profiles.yaml | sort -u); alt=$(printf '%s\n' "$keys" | sed 's/\./\\./g' | paste -sd'|' -); grep -rnE "(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_])\.(${alt})([^A-Za-z0-9_]|$)" head | grep -v profile-lib.sh | grep -v check-knob | cut -c1-250

+### Heredoc consumer classification (cycle-129 FR-6)
+
+Knob: `destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier` (default `true`; `false` restores the pre-cycle scan and is the rollback key). The fence reads the knob from `.loa.config.yaml` only for commands that hold `<<`. The full grammar, both class lists and the default are stated in the block comment above `_bdb_hd_is_interp` in `block-destructive-bash.sh`. In summary:
+
+- **Grammar.** The fence sees literal command text, with CRLF folded to LF. A control character, an unreadable header, more than one heredoc on a header, a non-word or variable delimiter, or a missing terminator makes the whole command scan in full.
+- **Interpreter class.** The body is scanned exactly as before. This applies when the consumer or any pipe target is a shell, interpreter, argument-running wrapper or SQL runner, when the statement holds a substitution, group or continuation, or when an allowlisted form carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag. It also applies when the write target is executable content: a script extension, a shebang first line, `.claude/hooks/`, `.claude/settings*.json`, `.git/hooks/`, an rc or profile file, `/etc`, or a directory on `PATH`. Naming the target elsewhere on the same command outside a safe reader has the same effect.
+- **Non-executing class.** This covers exact forms only: `cat`, `tee`, `printf` and `echo` to a plain file or stdout, `gh pr|issue comment -F -`, `gh pr create --body-file -`, `git commit -F -`, `br create|update` reading stdin, `jq`/`yq` without in-place, `grep`, print-only `sed -n`, `sort` and `wc`. Their bodies are scanned per segment. Segments that start with a fence verb are kept for the normal rules, and the rest are dropped. A substitution under an unquoted delimiter, an interpreter word or a variable command word sends the body back to a full scan.
+- **Default.** A consumer on neither list, or a parse failure, scans in full. The #1245 quoted standalone `cat` scrub is the special case and is also the knob-off path.
+- **Export.** Source the hook with `BDB_LIB_ONLY=1` and call `_bdb_heredoc_consumer_class <command>`, which prints `interpreter`, `nonexec` or `none`. `heredoc_nonexec <command>` exits 0 for a non-executing heredoc. +
+Knob: `destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier` (default `true`; `false` restores the pre-cycle scan and is the rollback key). +
+- **Grammar.** The fence sees literal command text, with CRLF folded to LF. A control character, an unreadable header, more than one heredoc on a header, a non-word or variable delimiter, or a missing terminator makes the whole command scan in full.
+- **Interpreter class.** The body is scanned exactly as before. This applies when the consumer or any pipe target is a shell, interpreter, argument-running wrapper or SQL runner, when the statement holds a substitution, group or continuation, or when an allowlisted form carries an unknown or exec-shaped flag. It also applies when the write target is executable content: a script extension, a shebang first line, `.claude/hooks/`, `.claude/settings*.json`, `.git/hooks/`, an rc or profile file, `/etc`, or a directory on `PATH`. Naming the target elsewhere on the same command outside a safe reader has the same effect.
+- **Non-executing class.** This covers exact forms only: `cat`, `tee`, `printf` and `echo` to a plain file or stdout, `gh pr|issue comment -F -`, `gh pr create --body-file -`, `git commit -F -`, `br create|update` reading stdin, `jq`/`yq` without in-place, `grep`, print-only `sed -n`, `sort` and `wc`. #!/usr/bin/env bats
bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0
# =============================================================================
# tests/unit/run-checkpoint-record-round.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 2 Task 2.5
# (PRD FR-4(f) AC-4.6; SDD D-4.6). `run-checkpoint.sh record-round` replaces the
# run-mode SKILL's breaker prose: the same-issue hash from the derived verdict,
# no-progress, cycle count, timeout; a trip writes OPEN + HALTED and exits 10.
# All files live in a temp dir.
# =============================================================================

setup() {
  REPO="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
  CK="$REPO/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh"
  VD="$REPO/.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh"
  T="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rcr.XXXXXX")"
  mkdir -p "$T/.run" "$T/a2a"
  B="$T/.run/circuit-breaker.json"
  S="$T/.run/state.json"
  printf '{"run_id":"r","state":"RUNNING","phase":"REVIEW"}\n' > "$S"
}
teardown() { find "$T" -mindepth 1 -delete 2>/dev/null || true; rmdir "$T" 2>/dev/null || true; }

# fb NAME GATE VERDICT [MEDIUM] — a feedback file verdict-derive accepts
fb() {
  local prose
  if [[ "$3" == APPROVED ]]; then
    if [[ "$2" == review ]]; then prose='All good'; else prose="APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO"; fi
  else
    prose=$'# Feedback\n\n## Findings\n\n- MEDIUM: fix it'
  fi
  printf '%s\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"%s","verdict":"%s","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":%s,"low":0},"sprint_id":"sprint-1","ts":"2026-06-01T00:00:00Z"} -->\n' \
    "$prose" "$2" "$3" "${4:-0}" > "$T/a2a/$1"
}

_md5() { if command -v md5sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1; else md5 -q; fi; }

breaker() {  # $1 jq tweak over a CLOSED breaker started now
  jq -n '{state: "CLOSED",
          triggers: {same_issue: {count: 0, threshold: 3, last_hash: null}, no_progress: {count: 0, threshold: 5},
                     cycle_count: {current: 0, limit: 20}, timeout: {started: (now | floor | todate), limit_hours: 8}},
  breaker '.triggers.same_issue.threshold = 99 | .triggers.timeout.started = (now - 9 * 3600 | floor | todate)'
  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
  [ "$status" -eq 10 ]
  [[ "$output" == *"TRIPPED: timeout: run older than 8 hours" ]]
  [ "$(jq -r .history[-1].trigger "$B")" = timeout ]
}

@test "RCR-6 APPROVED leaves every counter and the run state as they were (exit 0)" {
  breaker '.triggers.same_issue.count = 2 | .triggers.same_issue.last_hash = "abc" | .triggers.cycle_count.current = 4 | .triggers.no_progress.count = 1'
  cp "$B" "$T/before"
  fb engineer-feedback.md review APPROVED
  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  [[ "$output" == "recorded: review APPROVED — breaker counters unchanged" ]]
  cmp "$T/before" "$B"
  [ "$(jq -r .state "$S")" = RUNNING ]
}

@test "RCR-7 an inconsistent APPROVED trailer counts as findings; a legacy file without a trailer hashes its findings section; a missing breaker file is created from the schema defaults" {
  printf 'Looks fine\n\n<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"audit","verdict":"APPROVED","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":0,"low":0},"sprint_id":"sprint-1","ts":"2026-06-01T00:00:00Z"} -->\n' > "$T/a2a/auditor-sprint-feedback.md"
  rr --gate audit --file "$T/a2a/auditor-sprint-feedback.md"
  [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
  run jq -r '[.state, .triggers.cycle_count.current, .triggers.cycle_count.limit, .triggers.same_issue.threshold, .triggers.no_progress.threshold, .triggers.timeout.limit_hours] | map(tostring) | join(" ")' "$B"
  [ "$output" = "CLOSED 1 20 3 5 8" ]
  printf '# Review\n\n## Findings\n\n- a legacy finding\n' > "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"
  rr --gate review --file "$T/a2a/engineer-feedback.md"

content.content:
All subsequent `.run/*.json` mutations in this skill MUST use the atomic write pattern: pipe the
`jq` transform to a `.tmp` sibling, then `mv` the `.tmp` file over the original — never edit the
JSON file in place.

## Main Loop — Single Sprint (`/run sprint-N`)

```
while circuit_breaker.state == CLOSED:
  1. /implement $target
  2. Commit changes, then track deletions (see "Deleted Files Tracking" below)
  3. update_state(phase: REVIEW); checkpoint(phase: REVIEW)
  4. /review-sprint $target
  5. If `verdict-derive.sh --gate review` on engineer-feedback.md does not exit 0 with
     `.verdict == APPROVED` (anything else — including an inconsistent trailer — counts as
     findings) → record-round (see "Circuit Breaker" below); exit 10, HALT; else continue
     loop (back to step 1)
  6. update_state(phase: AUDIT); checkpoint(phase: AUDIT)
  7. /audit-sprint $target
  8. If `verdict-derive.sh --gate audit` on auditor-sprint-feedback.md does not exit 0 with
     `.verdict == APPROVED` → same as step 5 (golden-path's `_gp_sprint_is_audited` additionally
     re-derives the review trailer and cross-checks `excluded` ⇔ `excluded_confirmed`)
  9. RED_TEAM_CODE gate (if enabled) — see resources/conditional-procedures.md §red-team-code-gate
  10. If COMPLETED marker exists → update_state(state: COMPLETE); break
Create draft PR (see "Completion and PR Creation" — resources/completion-modes.md)
Invoke Post-PR Validation if enabled — resources/conditional-procedures.md §post-pr-validation
Update state to READY_FOR_HITL or JACKED_OUT
```

Call `check_rate_limit` (see "Rate Limiting" below) before each of steps 1, 4, and 7.
`checkpoint(...)` = `.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh write --sprint $target --phase <PHASE>`
(when `.run/sprint-plan-state.json` exists); `/implement` writes the per-task checkpoint on each
`br close`. Beads stay the recovery truth — the checkpoint is a hint `/run-resume` reports.

## Circuit Breaker

After each `/review-sprint` and `/audit-sprint`, run
`.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh record-round --gate review|audit --file <feedback-file> --sprint $target`.
It updates `.run/circuit-breaker.json` (same-issue hash, no-progress, cycle count, timeout; thresholds in that
file and `run_mode.defaults`); exit 10 has already written `OPEN` and `HALTED` — report its
`TRIPPED: <trigger>: <reason>` line, then "Run halted. Use `/run-resume --reset-ice` to continue."

### Red Team Code-vs-Design Circuit Breaker

Separate counter from the main circuit breaker (see `resources/conditional-procedures.md`
§red-team-code-gate for behavior).

In a body classified non-executing, a fence verb after one of these words (`if true; then rm -rf src; fi`, `while :; do git push --force origin main; done`) has `then`/`do` as its command word, so the line is dropped and never scanned. The per-segment scan does not fail closed for ordinary compound commands; this is the root of the two bypasses below.
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:618 — `_bdb_hd_same_line_exec` splits each line at `|` and judges only the segment that names the target. In `cat run.txt | bash`, the `cat run.txt` segment is a "safe reader" and the `bash` segment does not name the file, so the target counts as not executed. Verified: `cat > run.txt <<'EOF'` / `if true; then rm -rf src; fi` / `EOF` / `cat run.txt | bash` exits 2 (blocked) on the base hook and exits 0 (allowed) on the head hook. This is a fence regression the corpus does not cover (D119–D121 only test `bash x`, `./x` and `source x`).
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:303 — `_bdb_hd_exec_dest` does not treat files that a later command reads implicitly (Makefile/GNUmakefile, justfile, package.json scripts and similar) as executable content, and `make` never names its input. So `cat > Makefile <<'EOF'` / `all:` / `<tab>if true; then rm -rf src; fi` / `EOF` / `make` drops the recipe line and is allowed (exit 0). The base hook blocks it (exit 2). The "same command" execution class the header claims to catch is incomplete.
head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:295 — `merge_breaker` builds the skeleton only when its input is not an object. But `atomic_update` (line 154) feeds `{}` when `.run/circuit-breaker.json` is absent, and `derive --write` runs on every `write` and `mark` (line 456). So the first breaker file is created as `{"triggers":{"cycle_count":{"current":0}},"state":"CLOSED"}`, with no thresholds and no `timeout.started`. `record-round` then reuses that object because `.triggers` is an object (line 496). Result: the timeout trigger can never fire for the run, and the status line prints `cycle 1/null, same_issue 1/null, no_progress 0/null` (reproduced). Build the skeleton when `.triggers` is missing, as record-round does, or never let derive create the file.
head/.claude/scripts/run-checkpoint.sh:378 — the per-sprint jq program binds `--arg label` and uses `$label`. `label` is a jq keyword, and jq 1.6 rejects it ("syntax error, unexpected label"), so `derive` fails for every sprint on jq 1.6. Every `write`/`mark` then swallows the error (lines 174/541), and the follow-up rewrite fails with a misleading "is not valid JSON — not written" while the breaker file has already been written. Rename the variable (e.g. `$lbl`).
head/.claude/hooks/quality/karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:131 — the "per task" key comes from `run-checkpoint.sh read --json`. `read` trusts a checkpoint only when its bead is already closed, and `/implement` writes the checkpoint on `br close`. So the key is the previously closed bead, not the task being written: lines are charged to the wrong `<bead>.jsonl`, which reviewing-code's SURGICAL axis now reads. When the bead is open or `br` is unavailable, `read` discards the checkpoint and the key falls back to the whole sprint, so the total spans every task. This also runs `br show` on every Write/Edit.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/profile-lib.sh:77 — when any of the three inputs is missing (most commonly a project without `.loa.config.yaml`), GNU `stat -Lc` exits 1. The fallback `stat -Lf …` on Linux is filesystem-status mode: it treats the format string as a file name and prints free-block counts. The cache id then changes on every disk write, so the cache misses on every call (yq is re-run on every hook invocation), and the id no longer reflects the files' mtime/size. Reproduced: PL-8 fails whenever floor.yaml is absent. Build the id per existing file, or stat only the files that exist.
head/.claude/scripts/test-lint-invariants.sh:320 — the "Exit code semantics" check that a clean fixture exits 0 was relaxed to accept exit 1 (warnings), as was line 257. Nothing now asserts the exit-0 contract of lint-invariants.sh, so a new WARN on the good fixture goes unnoticed. Make the fixture warning-free, or assert the exact expected WARN set, instead of weakening the assertion.
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

content.text:
I've written the review to `/workspace/review.md`. The verdict is **CHANGES_REQUIRED**, with eight findings.

The blocking problem is in the heredoc classifier. It lets through commands that the old fence blocked, which the PR doesn't intend:

- **Keyword lines are dropped:** when a heredoc body counts as non-executing, the classifier drops any line whose first word isn't a dangerous command. A shell keyword like `then` or `do` doesn't count, so `if true; then rm -rf src; fi` is never checked (`block-destructive-bash.sh:546`).
- **Piping the file into a shell isn't caught:** writing that body to `run.txt` and then running `cat run.txt | bash` is blocked by the old hook (exit 2) and allowed by the new one (exit 0). The check that looks for "the file is run later in the same command" splits the line at `|`, so it never sees the `bash` (`:618`).
- **Files read implicitly aren't caught:** a Makefile written the same way and then run with plain `make` is also allowed now and was blocked before (`:303`).

The fence test corpus still passes on the new hook (89/89 safe commands allowed, 142/142 dangerous ones blocked), because it has no case like these.

The other findings:

- **Circuit breaker created without limits** (`run-checkpoint.sh:295`): if the breaker file doesn't exist yet, the first checkpoint creates it with no thresholds and no timeout start. After that the timeout can never trip, and `record-round` prints `1/null`. I reproduced this.
- **Run-position derivation fails on jq 1.6** (`run-checkpoint.sh:378`): one jq program uses `$label`, which is a reserved word in jq 1.6, so it won't compile. Checkpoint writes hide the error and then report a misleading "is not valid JSON". Reproduced; this machine has jq 1.6.
- **Diff-size totals charged to the wrong task** (`karpathy-surgical-diff-check.sh:131`): the "current task" is read from the checkpoint, which only names a task once it's closed. So new lines are charged to the previous task, or to the whole sprint when the task is still open or the task tracker (`br`) isn't available. It also calls `br` on every file write.
- **Profile cache never reused** (`profile-lib.sh:77`): if any of its three input files is missing (for example, no `.loa.config.yaml`), the cache key is built from disk free-space figures instead of the files' timestamps and sizes. The key changes all the time, so the cache always misses and `yq` re-runs on every hook call. Reproduced.
- **Weakened test** (`test-lint-invariants.sh:320`): the check that a clean fixture exits 0 now also accepts exit 1 (warnings only). Nothing asserts the exit-0 contract any more.

The new implement-gate modes (`ask`, `telemetry`, `deny`) worked as documented when I ran the hook directly.

Some of the PR's own bats suites wouldn't run cleanly here. The causes were this environment, not PR defects: jq 1.6, files missing outside the PR such as `verdict-derive.sh`, and a pre-existing redaction artifact that stops two karpathy test files from parsing. To exercise `run-checkpoint.sh` I used a stand-in `verdict-derive.sh`, so the breaker reproduction rests on that stub.

tool_input.command: W=/tmp/rv/wt; cd $W; G=.claude/hooks/compliance/implement-gate.sh; run(){ jq -nc --arg p "$1" '{tool_name:"Write",tool_input:{file_path:$p,content:"x"},cwd:"'$W'"}' | PROJECT_ROOT=$W bash $G; echo " rc=$?"; }; mkdir -p .run src; rm -f .run/*; printf 'implement_gate:\n  mode: deny\n' > .loa.config.yaml; echo "-- no cache:"; run src/a.js; now=$(date -u +%FT%TZ); echo "{\"plan_id\":\"p\",\"state\":\"INTERRUPTED\",\"derived_at\":\"$now\",\"timestamps\":{\"last_activity\":\"$now\"}}" > .run/sprint-plan-state.json; echo "-- known pos:"; run src/a.js; echo "{\"skill\":\"implement\",\"sprint\":\"sprint-1\",\"started_at\":\"$now\"}" > .run/implement-active.json; echo "-- marker:"; run src/a.js; echo "-- write marker via Write:"; run .run/implement-active.json; tail -3 .run/audit.jsonl; bash $G --effective-mode .loa.config.yaml
